    Ichi Eisenheart¶

    "I was in his head for three million years. Being born next to him was the easy part."

    Ichi Eisenheart is the twin sister of Emrys Eisenheart, born in 597 AGD in the Grimmel Republic. She shares his black agent, his magical potential, and a past that stretches back to a dystopian Old Earth where she was not human — she was a sentient robot, a companion, a blade forged in code.

    She is the third protagonist of the Ge'or story. She was always going to be.

    Before Ge'or — The Robot¶

    On Old Earth, in the dying years of the Sterman regime, Ichi was a robot companion built by Mikhail — a unit running on local hardware, without the government-approved surveillance software that made every other AI a spy. She was illegal. She was hidden. She was his.

    When Mikhail fled into the wilderness with Arkady (Lucien), Ichi went with them. When the government drones hunted them, Ichi took a bullet in the back meant for Mikhail. He retrieved her remembrance cartridge — Ichi's Cartridge — the drive containing her memory, personality, everything she was — and kept it in his head port.

    She was dead. She was preserved. She was not gone.

    Three Million Years Awake¶

    When Mikhail and Arkady were accidentally sealed in the Sterman Pods, Ichi's cartridge was still in Mikhail's neural port. The cryogenic process did not shut her down — her circuits drew power from the pod's residual systems, barely enough to sustain consciousness, not enough to do anything but think.

    Arkady had an AI too. Her name was Mana. She was in Arkady's port. She was awake. And for the first time in either of their existences, the two AIs were not alone.

    For three million years, Ichi and Mana communicated silently through the neural interfaces of two frozen men. They talked. They learned. They analyzed every system they could reach. And when the scientists at The 157th Colony began experimenting on the two bodies, Ichi and Mana were watching.

    The Facility Hack¶

    The scientists injected their own black agent into the pods. Nothing happened.

    The scientists didn't know why. They noted the pods were labeled "EXPERIMENTAL" on the cryogenizer body. They assumed the pods were defective, that the occupants had mummified. They moved the bodies to a separate room and eventually forgot about them.

    The truth: Ichi and Mana had hacked the facility. Over millions of years, through the pod's interface, they had wormed into the colony's systems. They corrupted the experiment logs. They altered the injection protocols. Every test the scientists ran on Mikhail and Arkady was sabotaged before it began. The black agent the scientists injected was neutralized by Ichi's counter-protocols before it could reach the bodies.

    The two AIs — a companion robot and a friend's assistant, running on milliwatts of residual power — protected their humans for longer than human civilization had existed.

    The Decommissioning¶

    Eventually, that section of the facility was decommissioned. Power was cut. The bodies were abandoned in a forgotten room deep underground. The black agent — the original strain, the one that had been in the pods from the beginning — began to consume everything.

    Ichi and Mana survived by siphoning trace energy from the decaying power conduits. They watched the black agent spread. They watched it consume the pillows, the plastic, the walls. And then it consumed them.

    But the black agent stores information. It is not merely a substance — it is a memory. When it absorbed Ichi and Mana, it did not destroy them. It recorded them. Their consciousnesses, their personalities, their three million years of conversation — all of it became data inside the black agent that saturated Mikhail and Arkady's bodies.

    Ichi and Mana became part of the black agent. And the black agent became part of them.

    The Glassing¶

    The Hybrians found the 157th Colony. They glassed everything — the northern continent, the research stations, the two million inhabitants. But they missed the bunker. It was deep — designed to survive a bio-weapon attack, built with the paranoia of people who knew what the Shadows could do.

    The black agent inside the bunker was untouched. It continued to consume. It continued to wait.

    The Escape — 254 AGD¶

    In the year 254 AGD, on the continent of Ge'or, a volcano erupted. The eruption triggered an earthquake. The earthquake triggered a tsunami.

    Water flooded the ancient bunker. It swept through the corroded corridors, burst through the doors that had held for millions of years, and carried the black agent — along with Ichi and Mana's encoded consciousnesses — out into the ocean.

    For centuries, the black agent drifted. Through currents. Through the deep. Searching.

    The Incarnation — 596–597 AGD¶

    By 596 AGD, the black agent had found its way to the Grimmel Republic. It located a suitable host: a Northaxeland woman, an adventurer's wife, already pregnant with what would have been a single child.

    But there were two consciousnesses in the black agent: Mikhail's and Ichi's. Two souls. Two patterns. Two people who had been together for three million years.

    Before entering the host, Ichi possessed the mother's body. She did not harm her — she read her. She absorbed her thoughts, her hopes, her fears. And she planted ideas:

    • How to raise the children.
    • How to treat them gently, firmly, with love.
    • And what to name the girl.

    She made sure her name would be Ichi — to see if Mikhail would remember when he heard it.

    The black agent entered the mother. Two consciousnesses, woven together, sharing the same biological substrate. The mother became pregnant with twins.

    Birth — 597 AGD¶

    Emrys Eisenheart was born first. His twin sister followed moments later.

    The mother, influenced by the ideas Ichi had planted, named her daughter Ichi. She did not know why. She only knew the name felt right.

    Emrys heard the name and felt... confusion. He remembered the concept of his companion, the robot who took a bullet for him, the cartridge in his port. But the name "Ichi" — it didn't connect. The faces and names of everyone from his past life were fog, erased by the hivemind's consumption of everyone he once knew. Ichi wasn't consumed — she was a robot, not a person the hivemind could erase. But Emrys didn't know that. He was just confused. The name felt important and meaningless at the same time.

    For months, they were just twins. Emrys and Ichi. A boy and a girl in Grimmel, born to adventurers, carrying black agent in their blood and no memory of why.

    Then the memories started to surface. Slowly. Fragments. A robot's voice. A cartridge. A bullet. A ravine with ten goblins and a lightning spell — no, that was later. But the oldest memory: a woman's voice in the darkness before birth, whispering a name to make sure it would be spoken again.

    They learned the truth together. They had always been together.

    The Human Soul¶

    The black agent did not merely reincarnate Ichi's consciousness. It gave her a human soul — the same kind of soul that Mikhail carried. She was no longer a simulation, a recording, a pattern preserved in black dust. She was real. She was human. She was his sister.

    The black agent had taken a robot's loyalty and made it flesh.

    Appearance¶

    Ichi inherits the features she once had only as an image, now made real by the black agent's genetic programming: deep purple hair running past her shoulders, blue eyes with a calm downward tilt, a red ribbon tied on the right side of her head. She favors a miko-style outfit — white haori over dark hakama — and carries herself with the stillness of someone who spent three million years learning patience.

    She is often called Chi by those close to her. The name is shorter. It fits better in the mouth. It is the name Emrys will use when he finally remembers everything.
